2026-09-23T13:03:18.7443989Z **Creating a Pull Request**
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7445699Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7445832Z To create a pull request:
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7446176Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7446869Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7449698Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7450557Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7451221Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7452150Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7452659Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7454340Z **Important**: The `branch` parameter in the create_pull_request tool **must exactly match the name of your current local git branch** — the branch you just committed to. You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7455881Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7456810Z **Important**: `create_pull_request` is not a sandbox. Every successful call records a real PR intent that can become an externally visible pull request. 2026-09-23T13:03:18.7472527Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7473174Z For `safeoutputs`, every successful call is a real write-intent declaration - do not use it for probing, auth checks, or placeholder payloads. Use `noop` or `report_incomplete` if not ready to emit the final action.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7473870Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7474122Z For multiple or complex arguments, pipe a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel:
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7474541Z ```bash
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7474913Z printf '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody."}' | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7475625Z # or write to a file: safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7476005Z ```
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7476110Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7478782Z **Multi-line or long `body` content:** do NOT build the JSON payload with `printf`/`echo` embedding raw newlines or many escaped characters directly in the command line — the sandbox's shell command-injection guard may reject long or complex quoted arguments (reporting "expansion patterns"/"command substitution" even though none are present) and retrying the identical command will fail again. Instead, write the content to a temp file with a heredoc, then use `jq -Rs` to inject it as the `body` field:
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7481944Z ```bash
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7482169Z cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gh-aw/body.md
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7482672Z Title
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7483024Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7483128Z Multi-line body content goes here.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7483637Z EOF
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7484217Z jq -Rs '{title: "My title", body: .}' /tmp/gh-aw/body.md | safeoutputs create_discussion .
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7485404Z ```
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7486561Z If a shell command is rejected for containing expansion patterns, do not retry the same command — switch to the heredoc + `jq -Rs` pattern above.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7487314Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7488865Z To inject an entire local file as the `body` field without re-embedding its content in the model context, use `jq -Rs`:
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7489617Z ```bash
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7490106Z jq -Rs --arg discussion_number "$DISCUSSION_NUMBER" \
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7490740Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7491339Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7491599Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7492102Z ```
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7494580Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7496358Z 
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7497353Z The generated command syntax above is schema-derived from each enabled tool's final `inputSchema` and is the source of truth for required/optional parameters.
2026-09-23T13:03:18.7498787Z Use `<server> --help` and `<server> <tool> --help` for the same schema-derived signatures and examples before calling any command.
